indicator_definition: This indicator measures the proportion of adults aged 15 and over who currently smoke tobacco products (including cigarettes, cigars and pipes) on a daily or occasional basis. It is expressed as a percentage of the total adult population. Data are collected through the European Health Interview Survey (EHIS).
rationale: Tobacco use is the leading preventable cause of death globally, causing cancer, cardiovascular disease and chronic respiratory conditions. Reducing smoking prevalence is a key public health priority. Progress means a sustained decline in the proportion of adults who smoke.
methodology_characteristics: Data are collected through the European Health Interview Survey (EHIS), conducted approximately every five years. Smoking status is self-reported. The survey uses a standardised questionnaire enabling cross-country comparisons across all EU member states and participating countries.
